parameters.content:
## onchain-error-alert
Error Trigger → **Normalize Input** (Set: owns the error-payload→named-fields contract + the target `ChatID`, with fallbacks so nothing renders `undefined`) → Telegram → **Record delivery → Write delivery**. Set as the `errorWorkflow` for onchain-* workflows; fires a Telegram alert on any failure. To change the target chat or the message, edit **Normalize Input** — not the Telegram node.

**HTML-escaping is load-bearing (L-4).** The Telegram node sends `parse_mode: HTML`, and the fields interpolated here are arbitrary vendor/runtime text. A raw `_` is an italic delimiter under Telegram's Markdown modes and a raw `<` breaks HTML mode — either way an unparseable entity means **400 and NO alert delivered**, i.e. the alerting path fails exactly when it is needed. `workflow_name` / `last_node` / `error_message` are escaped here (`&` first), and `error_message` is capped at 1500 chars so a long stack trace cannot blow the 4096-char message limit. Keep both when editing.

**The heartbeat (WI-64).** This workflow cannot report its own failure — it IS the reporter, and L-21 is what that costs: nine alerts failed over five days and the silence was found by accident. So every CONFIRMED send writes an `alert.delivered` row into `onchain.diagnostics` (least-privileged **Onchain engine state** credential), and **onchain-verify** reads the newest row's age daily against `AlertHeartbeatMaxAgeMs`. The write is CHAINED after Telegram, never fanned out beside it: only a delivery Telegram accepted counts. These rows are the extra pulse — this workflow runs only on failures, so onchain-verify's own daily report writes the regular one.

Owner: onchain-intel.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO onchain.diagnostics
  (id, ts, severity, event, principal_id, session_id, provider, capability, trace_id, detail_json, created_at)
SELECT id, ts, severity, event, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, detail_json, created_at
FROM jsonb_to_recordset(convert_from(decode($1,'base64'),'utf8')::jsonb)
  AS x(id text, ts bigint, severity text, event text, detail_json text, created_at bigint);
